documents: Passport, second ID, proof of foreign address, bank/professional reference letters, proof of income and source-of-wealth documentation, stated reason for banking in the Bahamas.
min_deposit_fees: Varies by bank; guides cite roughly USD 10,000-250,000 for non-resident/offshore accounts, higher for private banking; fees not published.
banks: Mainly international/private banks rather than retail banks; specific accepting banks not confirmed from official pages.
restrictions: Exchange controls administered by the Central Bank of The Bahamas; only authorised dealers may offer foreign-currency accounts; strong CRS/FATCA and AML scrutiny, many retail banks serve residents only.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut from Australia for multi-currency needs; offshore private banks elsewhere.
cost_note: Guides cite USD 10,000-250,000 minimum for non-resident/offshore accounts at international/private banks (low end used, already USD); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport with valid entry stamp, second ID, proof of foreign address, home-bank reference letter (often in Spanish), proof of income/source of funds, FATCA/CRS forms.
min_deposit_fees: Low; guides cite about USD 100-500 opening deposit (Banreservas USD account reported around USD 300); monthly fees not published.
banks: Banco Popular Dominicano, Banreservas, BHD, Scotiabank (practice varies by branch).
restrictions: Usually savings accounts only for non-residents; branch-level discretion and frequent refusals; overstayed tourists cannot open; withdrawal limits and fees vary.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut for transfers; local remittance services.
cost_note: Banreservas USD account reported at about USD 300 opening deposit (guides cite USD 100-500, already USD); opening and monthly fees are not published for non-residents.

documents: Passport plus second ID, one or two bank reference letters, professional reference, proof of address, proof of income, source-of-funds statement, CV; remote applications usually need notarised or apostilled copies.
min_deposit_fees: Varies widely; guides cite about USD 1,000-10,000, some banks up to USD 250,000 for non-residents; fees not published.
banks: Specific accepting banks not confirmed from official pages; acceptance is bank-by-bank and often via a local attorney introduction.
restrictions: Heavy AML/KYC due diligence and frequent unexplained rejections; FATCA forms for US persons; dollarised economy so USD accounts are standard.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Panama-based EMIs not established for non-residents.
cost_note: Guides cite USD 1,000-10,000 (some banks up to USD 250,000) minimum for non-residents, low end used and already in USD; opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Paraguayan cedula (national ID) normally required, plus passport, local address, proof of income and source-of-funds/patrimony declaration.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for passport-only non-residents; Banco Atlas and Banco Continental require a cedula for full personal accounts.
restrictions: Since 2026 banks require origin-of-funds and patrimony declarations; tourists generally rejected; non-residents can usually bank only via a Paraguayan company with an RUC.
alternatives: Obtain residency and cedula first; otherwise Wise or Revolut from abroad.
cost_note: Not applicable: passport-only non-residents cannot open personal accounts (Banco Atlas and Banco Continental require a cedula), so no costs apply.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign residential address, proof of income/source of funds, purpose of account; some banks also ask for tax residency (CRS) self-certification and an in-person visit.
min_deposit_fees: HSBC One charges non-HKID holders HKD 100/month below HKD 10,000 balance (from Jan 2026); Premier requires a high balance (not published here); other banks not published.
banks: HSBC Hong Kong (international/remote onboarding for residents of designated countries; existing Premier clients qualify automatically); other banks case-by-case.
restrictions: No capital controls and HKD/USD freely available, but strict AML/KYC; virtual banks generally require a HKID; many banks require a branch visit and reject non-residents without clear HK nexus.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut HKD details; Statrys/Airwallex for business only.
cost_note: HSBC One charges non-HKID holders HKD 100/month when the balance is below HKD 10,000 (about USD 1,280) at roughly 0.128 USD/HKD; no opening fee or opening minimum is published.

documents: Passport with valid Lao visa, proof of local address in Laos; work permit for some products such as BCEL i-Bank; source-of-funds for investors.
min_deposit_fees: not published; foreign-investor accounts may require USD 10,000 where ministries or the bank require it.
banks: BCEL (Banque pour le Commerce Exterieur Lao) is most cited for foreigners; others not confirmed.
restrictions: Bank of Lao PDR rules allow non-resident foreign-currency accounts with a passport, but banks typically want a visa and local address; foreign-currency shortages and exchange controls on kip.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut from Australia; cash/remittance services.
cost_note: Not published: BCEL personal-account opening fees, minimum deposit and monthly fees for non-residents are unpublished (the USD 10,000 figure applies only to some foreign-investor accounts).

documents: Passport, proof of local physical address (PO Box not accepted), residence or work permit usually expected, plus AML/CFT source-of-funds information.
min_deposit_fees: Guides cite about TOP 100-300 opening deposit for a standard account; fees not published.
banks: ANZ Tonga, BSP Tonga, Tonga Development Bank (non-resident policy not published).
restrictions: Small market with AML/CFT de-risking; non-residents face significant challenges and banks prefer a branch visit in Nuku'alofa.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Australian or NZ bank accounts with remittance to Tonga.
cost_note: Guides cite about TOP 100-300 opening deposit for a standard account at ANZ/BSP Tonga, low end TOP 100 at about 0.42 USD/TOP; opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, sometimes proof of foreign address and source-of-funds documents; remote opening usually via notarised/apostilled power of attorney.
min_deposit_fees: Low; no significant minimum deposit at retail banks, small annual service fees (not published here); intermediary POA services cost extra.
banks: TBC Bank, Bank of Georgia, Liberty Bank, Space Bank (app onboarding for some nationalities).
restrictions: No legal bar on foreigners but KYC tightened in 2026 with source-of-funds checks; some nationalities restricted; multi-currency GEL/USD/EUR accounts allowed.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut; Space Bank app (TBC) for eligible nationalities.
cost_note: Bank of Georgia Basic package: free current-account opening, no stated minimum balance, GEL 5/month for non-residents (GEL 2 for residents) at about 0.37 USD/GEL.

documents: Cameroonian residence permit, taxpayer card (NIU), passport, proof of local address; non-resident accounts mainly for legal entities.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-resident individuals.
restrictions: BEAC/CEMAC foreign-exchange regulation controls non-resident and foreign-currency accounts tightly; residence is the first condition for foreigners per local lawyers.
alternatives: Mobile money (MTN MoMo, Orange Money) needs a local SIM and ID; Wise/Revolut from abroad.
cost_note: Not applicable: no known bank opens personal accounts for non-resident individuals, so no costs apply.

documents: Passport, residence permit, proof of local address or residence registration, employment/assignment letter, TIN if available.
min_deposit_fees: Initial deposit varies by bank; not published.
banks: none known for non-residents; CRDB Bank Burundi, BANCOBU, BCB and KCB Burundi require branch KYC.
restrictions: Visitor visa not sufficient; strict foreign-exchange controls and chronic USD shortages; diaspora accounts limited to Burundian nationals.
alternatives: Mobile money (Lumicash, Ecocash) requires local SIM/ID; Wise/Revolut from abroad.
cost_note: Not applicable: non-residents cannot open accounts remotely (branch KYC required at CRDB, BANCOBU, BCB, KCB), and initial deposits are not published.

documents: Passport with work or residence visa or resident card, Angolan tax number (NIF), proof of address; investors need BNA-regulated investor account documentation.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for ordinary non-resident individuals; non-resident investor accounts possible at local commercial banks.
restrictions: Non-resident kwanza accounts are regulated foreign-exchange operations under BNA rules (Notice 1/23); visa required for foreigners; FX controls and USD scarcity.
alternatives: Wise/Revolut from abroad; Unitel Money/e-Kwanza require local ID.
cost_note: Not applicable: ordinary non-resident individuals cannot open personal accounts, and no fees are published.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address (certificate of residence or utility bill under 3 months), proof of income; some banks want a Luxembourg employment contract or payslips.
min_deposit_fees: Retail accounts have small monthly package fees (not published here); private banks typically require high minimum assets (not published).
banks: Spuerkeess (BCEE) explicitly accepts non-residents incl. digital onboarding; BGL BNP Paribas partially digital; private banks for wealthier clients.
restrictions: Some banks serve only residents or cross-border workers; digital onboarding excluded for AML/compliance flags; EU AML and CRS reporting to ATO.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (EUR IBAN) without residency.
cost_note: Spuerkeess Zebra package is EUR 3.50/month (EUR 42/year, fee information document dated April 2024) at about 1.15 USD/EUR; no opening fee or minimum deposit is published there.

documents: Passport; often a PESEL number (obtainable for tax purposes), proof of foreign address, sometimes tax residence certificate; branch visit or video verification.
min_deposit_fees: Basic accounts often free or low monthly fee (around PLN 0-10, varies by bank); not published for non-residents specifically.
banks: PKO Bank Polski, mBank, Bank Millennium, Santander Bank Polska, Bank Pekao (practice varies).
restrictions: Many banks insist on PESEL and branch visit; EU AML checks and CRS reporting; no capital controls.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (Polish-licensed EU bank) with PL IBAN.
cost_note: Not published for non-residents: basic personal accounts at PKO BP, mBank and others run about PLN 0-10/month (about USD 0-2.7 at 0.27 USD/PLN), but no bank publishes a specific non-resident tariff.

documents: Valid foreign passport (or EU/Schengen ID), completed application, source-of-funds information; power of attorney signed abroad must be apostilled.
min_deposit_fees: Small monthly maintenance fees; exact non-resident tariffs not published here.
banks: Komercijalna Banka Skopje (published non-resident conditions); other banks such as Stopanska Banka case-by-case.
restrictions: Non-resident accounts are FX current accounts (with MKD use permitted) under National Bank rules; remote opening generally unavailable; enhanced due diligence on origin of funds.
alternatives: Wise or Revolut from abroad.
cost_note: Not published: Komercijalna Banka's non-resident general conditions refer to its tariff without giving opening, minimum-balance or monthly amounts.

documents: Passport, recent proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, proof of income and source of funds, evidence of ties to Malta and purpose of account.
min_deposit_fees: not published; non-Europeans may face higher fees.
banks: Bank of Valletta (branch appointment, strict onboarding), HSBC Malta (online start but branch ID check, mainly Malta/EU residents).
restrictions: Strong de-risking after FATF grey-listing era; 2-8 week processing; non-EU applicants face extra scrutiny and frequent refusals.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (EUR IBAN); Maltese EMIs mainly for business.
cost_note: Not published: Bank of Valletta and HSBC Malta do not publish non-resident opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees.

documents: Passport, Latvian residence permit or documented connection to Latvia (employment, study, property, business), proof of income and source of funds, tax returns/statements.
min_deposit_fees: Non-resident fees can be high; specifics not published.
banks: Swedbank, SEB, Citadele (each requires a connection to Latvia for non-residents).
restrictions: Heavy de-risking of non-resident clients since the ABLV money-laundering cases; remote onboarding only for Latvian ID/eID holders.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, Lithuanian EMIs.
cost_note: Not published: Swedbank, SEB and Citadele levy higher non-resident fees but the specific amounts are not published.

documents: Passport with Syrian entry/temporary residence stamp, local address, ID copies; in-person visit in Damascus.
min_deposit_fees: Cham Bank current account minimum SYP 10,000 or FX equivalent; others not published.
banks: none known for remote non-residents; Cham Bank and Bank Audi Syria accept non-Syrians only in person.
restrictions: US and EU economic sanctions lifted 2025-2026 and SWIFT reconnected Nov 2025, but correspondent banking and USD access remain very limited; liquidity withdrawal limits.
alternatives: Realistically bank via Lebanese, Jordanian, Turkish or Gulf banks; Wise/Revolut not available for Syria transfers in most cases.
cost_note: Not applicable: remote non-residents cannot open accounts; Cham Bank's in-person current-account minimum is SYP 10,000 or FX equivalent, a negligible amount at current rates.

documents: Palestinian or Jerusalem ID typically required, plus residence evidence; foreign companies must be registered with the Companies Registrar.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known; Bank of Palestine reportedly requires a Palestinian/Jerusalem ID.
restrictions: Banking depends on Israeli correspondent arrangements and shekel cash constraints; PMA classifies non-residents strictly; Gaza banking severely disrupted by conflict.
alternatives: Jordanian banks (e.g. in Amman) or Israeli banks serve most cross-border needs; local wallets like PalPay need local ID.
cost_note: Not applicable: Bank of Palestine reportedly requires a Palestinian/Jerusalem ID, so non-residents cannot open accounts and no costs apply.

documents: Residence or work permit for foreigners; diaspora FX accounts require Ethiopian nationality or Ethiopian origin (yellow card).
min_deposit_fees: Diaspora accounts: USD 100 minimum (USD 5,000 fixed deposit); not applicable to other foreigners.
banks: none known for non-resident foreigners without Ethiopian origin; Commercial Bank of Ethiopia and others offer diaspora accounts only.
restrictions: Strict NBE foreign-exchange controls; FX accounts limited to resident foreigners, diaspora and approved entities (FDI firms, embassies, NGOs).
alternatives: Wise/remittance services into Ethiopia; telebirr requires local ID/SIM.
cost_note: Not applicable: non-resident foreigners without Ethiopian origin cannot open accounts; diaspora accounts (USD 100 minimum, USD 5,000 fixed deposit) do not apply.

documents: Passport, proof of non-resident status (foreign visa/residence, entry/exit stamps), proof of profession and source of funds, CRS/FATCA forms.
min_deposit_fees: Roshan Digital Accounts have no or low minimum balance; fees not published for foreign nationals.
banks: Roshan Digital Account banks including HBL (NRAN account lists foreign nationals as eligible) and Standard Chartered Pakistan; others mainly require Pakistani CNIC/NICOP/POC.
restrictions: SBP rules allow non-resident foreign nationals into RDA, but many banks limit products to Pakistani-origin customers; FX controls on outward remittances; FATF scrutiny.
alternatives: Wise to PKR accounts; JazzCash/Easypaisa need a Pakistani CNIC.
cost_note: Not published: Roshan Digital Accounts (e.g. HBL) are described as having no or low minimum balance, but opening and monthly fees for foreign nationals are not published.

documents: Passport, proof of address, residence permit or carte de sejour usually requested, source-of-funds; non-resident and foreign-currency accounts need BCEAO/Treasury formalities.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-WAEMU non-residents; diaspora accounts (BCEAO Notice 001-03-2026) cover WAEMU nationals only.
restrictions: BCEAO exchange controls; foreign-currency accounts require Finance Ministry/BCEAO authorisation; non-resident operations subject to prior authorisation.
alternatives: Mobile money (Orange Money, MTN MoMo, Wave) requires local SIM and ID; Wise from abroad.
cost_note: Not published: no known option for non-WAEMU non-residents, and no bank publishes non-resident fees.

documents: Passport, proof of address, photo, residence permit if applicable, TIN if available; branch visit with ID.
min_deposit_fees: Initial deposit varies by bank; not published.
banks: Rokel Commercial Bank and others require branch visit; Ecobank Sierra Leone policy not published.
restrictions: Bank of Sierra Leone permits residents and non-residents to hold foreign-currency accounts, but banks rarely onboard non-residents remotely; AML de-risking.
alternatives: Orange Money and Afrimoney need local SIM/ID; Wise/remittance services from abroad.
cost_note: Not published: Rokel Commercial Bank and others require a branch visit, and initial deposits and fees are not published.
